title: sdks: unify auth/retries/streaming ergonomics across Python/TS/Go + parity/version bumps
author: Priya Shah
release_notes: Unified SDK ergonomics across Python/TypeScript/Go: standardized auth API, default retry/backoff parity, aligned streaming APIs, minor telemetry parity; bumped SDK versions to 1.7.0; no breaking changes for public surface except renamed internal helpers.
description: Context: We have divergent ergonomics and defaults across the three official SDKs which causes confusion for new customers and extra maintenance burden. This PR standardizes auth initialization, retry/backoff defaults, and streaming API shapes across Python, TypeScript, and Go. Motivation: consistent cross-language developer experience, easier documentation and examples, and fewer platform-specific bugs. What this PR does: - Introduces a shared AuthClient contract and adapts each SDK to the same initialization flow (token provider + optional KMS hooks). - Normalizes retry behavior and default backoffs (exponential with jitter, max_retries=4, initial_backoff=100ms) across SDKs. - Aligns streaming APIs: Python async iterator + context manager, TypeScript async iterable + event emitter shim, Go channel-based generator with CancelContext. - Fixes parity issues: metadata propagation for telemetry, consistent error types for HTTP 429/503, and unified header names. - Bumps package versions (python/typescript/go) to 1.7.0 and updates changelogs. - Adds tests and e2e streaming harness runs. Checklist: [x] design doc linked (ENG-1432) [x] unit tests added/updated [x] integration/e2e streaming run [x] changelogs updated [x] docs snippets updated (samples) [x] version bumps ready to release Caveats: there are no API-breaking changes for most users; internal helpers renamed (see migration notes in changelog).
commits: 7 commits: 1) sdk: add shared AuthClient interface and adapters (python/ts/go) 2) sdk: normalize retry/backoff defaults and implement exponential jitter 3) python: streaming iterator + context manager and tests 4) typescript: async iterable streaming API + emitter shim 5) go: channel-based generator + context cancellation and docs 6) docs: update samples and changelogs 7) release: bump versions and lockfiles
